content.title: Roman Reigns Addresses Rumor He Had Another Child During WWE Hiatus
content.text: "WWE Raw" after WrestleMania 42 arrived this Monday, April 20, as WWE stuck around in Las Vegas, moving over to the T-Mobile Arena after two nights in Allegiant Stadium. To follow up on the big weekend, WWE delivered plenty of its usual surprises to set the path forward until next April.Family Matters (Wrestling Edition)One day into his new reign as the World Heavyweight Champion, Roman Reigns stayed true to his promise of a return to full-time status. The champion closed the show by teasing business, only to pivot into what he always does best: Family manipulation with just enough sincerity to blur the lines of how evil he currently is.Reigns went out to the ring alongside The Usos, admitting they're all weaker apart and extending a more open-handed approach than usual with recent Bloodline teases. Less dictator, more “we need each other” — that was the vibe. Of course, he still couldn’t help but slide in a stray shot at CM Punk, thanks to the former champ's truthful digs throughout their pre-WrestleMania feud.Jimmy Uso spoke for his brother and reaffirmed their loyalty before the segment found its teeth.Unfortunately, it wasn't Oba Femi who interrupted after opening the night. ("The Ruler" started Monday's show by proclaiming that he had arrived, and then left. It would've been a perfect swerve to have this red-hot future champion strap on the rockets tonight and attack Reigns in the closing moments.)Instead, it was Jacob Fatu, sticking to the family dynamic.There wasn't an acknowledgment from "The Samoan Werewolf." Hell, he didn't even feign interest in becoming “Tribal Chief” like Solo Sikoa did. He just wants everything that comes with it.Excuse me: He "needs" it.The title. The money. The life. Fatu made it very family-centric — but just for his immediate family. That was a refreshingly grounded motivation, highlighted by an offhand (and genuinely funny) mention of Reigns’ shoe deal before Fatu pivoted to providing for his loved ones. It made Fatu feel like a man chasing opportunity at any cost ... even if that means putting down his own Bloodline relatives.Does it make a ton of sense? Not entirely. Fatu had laid a pre-Mania foundation with Cody Rhodes as part of his Drew McIntyre feud — revisiting that would've made for a more immediate, logical turn, especially since they didn't even get a match. Yes, Reigns brings the family drama, but are we clamoring for this? With Femi standing right there? Not exactly.Reigns, as always, played it perfectly, planting doubt and questioning Fatu’s ability to carry the burden of being a world champ. Then he left the door open with the classic “think about it” tease, kicking the can down the road until next Monday. This felt like a full-on revisit to 2023. For better or worse.Back at it againPunk’s promo was one of the more human moments of the night. At least in terms of really pulling back the curtain and speaking naturally in every sense.Between shouting out the departed Duke Roufus, his dog Larry, and others behind the scenes, it felt grounded in the real-life losses within Punk's life, before circling back to storyline frustration after dropping the title on Sunday. The crowd stayed with him, after initially showering him with boos, even when he veered into recap territory.Then came a wild Rhodes, visibly beaten down and bruised.Their exchange was simple, but effective — far more than what we saw last Friday. Punk reinforcing that losses happen, especially against people you care about, while subtly keeping himself in the title picture was clean work. Rhodes fired back without beating around the bush.“Just say when,” he said of Punk's potential "title opportunity out of thin air."As I stated last Friday, this is the match. This is the feud. No need to overthink it, folks. Please, WWE, just don’t drag it out for months on end — at least their first match. Clearly, this is as WrestleMania of a program as WWE could ask for, and arguably should've been done this year. But waiting until next April for their first match would be wild. It's one of those that doesn't even necessarily need the title.Speaking of that, Rhodes brought his title out tonight. I wonder how he took it back from Randy Orton.Snatching soulsLiv Morgan and Sol Ruca delivered the night’s standout between-the-ropes action, and I'm oh-so-happy to say that.It wasn't Ruca's official call-up to the main roster, as she still has her "Last Woman Standing" match with Zaria tomorrow on NXT. But Ruca had the perfect opportunity to continue showing why she's the company's breakout waiting to happen — if she hasn't already. The athleticism, the creativity (that handstand Oblivion escape was ridiculous), and the crowd connection are all there. Morgan, as expected, played her role perfectly. She bumped and sold great for the NXT star, and kept the pace sharp.The interference finish wasn’t ideal, but it worked very, very well for the story provided. Zaria cost Ruca the match, and nearly got her counted out, which probably protects Ruca a bit more. Losing to the new world champion isn't the worst blow whatsoever, and it didn’t take away from what was otherwise a great showcase.Afterward, Stephanie Vaquer stepped back into the mix. The only reason I'm OK with this is for the fact that it will hopefully give the pair a match with time — unlike their sub-seven-minute duel at 'Mania. They both deserve far better, and WWE may realize that by keeping the feud going — for now.EgomaniacRuca wasn't the only NXT surprise of the night. Ethan Page was first to arrive and made his official main roster debut.His rookie win over Je'Von Evans came with unexpected help from Rusev, but showed off his overall strength and gave him an immediate place in the mix. Watching Page stand back while Rusev handled the destruction was a nice character touch, especially for those unfamiliar with him. He’s here for himself. That much is clear.In the end, Rusev stood tall after Accolades on Evans and Penta, who attempted to help make the save. This feels like a clear-cut Fatal-4-Way match for the Intercontinental Championship waiting to happen.Breakking logicThe night’s messiest thread belonged to Bron Breakker and Seth Rollins — literally. Poor Breakker just returned from injury, and now he gets the back of his skull busted open to spread plasma across the ring.After an emotional sendoff for Brock Lesnar from Paul Heyman, "The Wiseman" focused on The Vision, as Logan Paul remained a heat magnet. His quick-hypocrite promo work was fine, but a side beat from the real story.Breakker arrived shortly after, and really, the more I think about it, he has no good reason for targeting Rollins and wanting to make Rollins' life hell, as he claimed to pursue. It still doesn’t quite add up.The intensity is there, but the logic? Not so much. He — as far as we know — was willingly recruited into The Vision by Heyman. Rollins never manipulated him like, let's say, Reigns and the Usos. All he did was steal the spotlight. You're free, man. Why does it matter now?Ultimately, things broke down into Rollins retaliating from his 'Mania loss with a chair shot to the back of Breakker's head — the source of the blood flow. The brawl worked, and Rollins was beaten down, including a pair of Breakker spears. But to run off Austin Theory and Paul, The Street Profits returned to even the odds.Fun? Sure. Logical? Not in the moment. Not at all.Obviously, the Profits will reveal their motivation next week, boiling it down to a desire for the World Tag Team Championships. That's fine enough. It just felt oddly timed, and a trios match is now guaranteed sooner rather than later.👑 Uncrowned Gem of the Night 👑Lesnar may actually be that guy who won't be enticed back for one more match, even for a hometown showcase later this year at SummerSlam. At least that's how WWE is leaning into it as of now, as they delivered a vintage tribute package for truly one of the all-time greats. Love him or hate him, this Lesnar video package was as good as it gets.I give Monday’s "Raw" a crown score of: 👑 8/10 👑WWE Raw full card results:Finn Balor def. JD McDonagh — 👑 2.5/5 👑Liv Morgan def. Sol Ruca — 👑 4/5 👑Ethan Page def. Je'Von Evans — 👑 3.25/5 👑RHIYO (Rhea Ripley and Iyo Sky) def. The Kabuki Warriors (Asuka and Kairi Sane) — 👑 3/5 👑Recap "WWE Raw" with Uncrowned's live blog:Live coverage is over62 updates
